quick_skim.title: Active Reachability Learning for Humanoid Recoverability Monitoring
quick_skim.abstract: Deploying humanoid task policies requires reliable runtime monitors that anticipate unrecoverable falls in time to trigger a fallback. We formulate this task as learning the stochastic, finite-horizon recoverability envelope of a given fallback policy. Synthesizing this monitor is challenging: existing methods assume training data naturally covers the recoverability envelope, yet acquiring such data remains a major bottleneck for contact-rich systems. Consequently, they recover only a fraction of the true envelope, leaving them prone to optimistic hallucinations for out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. We resolve this via a unified framework that iterates between value learning and active exploration. Data exploration is reframed as a reach-avoid problem, where an uncertainty-guided explorer systematically uncovers unseen states while avoiding confidently unrecoverable regions. This loop is further supported by a combined Temporal Difference and Monte Carlo objective for accurate in-distribution value prediction and reliable uncertainty estimation. By explicitly treating the remaining high-uncertainty regions as unrecoverable, the monitor mitigates optimistic OOD hallucinations. Evaluated on stochastic benchmarks and a 29-DoF Unitree G1 humanoid, our approach drastically improves monitor coverage and accuracy and successfully transfers zero-shot to real-world hardware.

quick_skim.title: Graph-Convolutional Reinforcement Learning for Finite-Time Stabilization of a Chaotic Chua Circuit via Unified Flexible Terminal Sliding-Mode Control
quick_skim.abstract: This paper introduces a graph convolutional reinforcement learning framework for the finite-time stabilization of chaotic dynamics in a physical Chua circuit. The circuit is modeled directly in terms of capacitor voltages, inductor current, and physical component parameters. This preserves the connection between the mathematical model and the underlying electrical system. A unified, flexible terminal sliding-mode controller is developed to achieve stabilization within a finite time in the presence of uncertainties in the lumped model, external disturbances, and bounded control inputs. The controller incorporates state-dependent nonlinear exponents to provide flexible convergence characteristics while avoiding singular terms near equilibrium. To minimize dependence on manual controller tuning, the admissible controller parameters are optimized using an actor-critic reinforcement learning scheme with a graph convolutional network that leverages the circuit dynamics' coupling structure. The learned parameters are constrained to the ranges required by the theoretical stability conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the rapid suppression of chaotic oscillations and the finite-time convergence of the state and sliding variables while respecting the prescribed input-saturation limits. Compared to a reference control method, the proposed approach reduces the IAE, ISE, ITAE, and ITSE by 56.27\,\%, 56.40\,\%, 61.69\,\%, and 64.70\,\%, respectively. These results suggest that graph-based reinforcement learning can effectively tune parameters while retaining the robustness and analytical structure of the underlying sliding-mode controller.

quick_skim.title: Tokens of Motion: Primitive Motion Learning for Human-Humanoid Skill Transfer
quick_skim.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models provide a promising paradigm for scalable robotic manipulation, yet their reliance on success-only behavioral cloning leaves them brittle; lacking corrective training signals, minor execution errors rapidly compound into unrecoverable, out-of-distribution failures. To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning (AFIL), an end-to-end framework that leverages failure trajectories as adaptive negative guidance for diffusion- and flow-based VLA policies. AFIL uses a pretrained VLA to generate failure rollouts online, avoiding the need for handcrafted failure-mode design or human-in-the-loop recovery. It then jointly trains Dual Action Generators (DAGs) for successful and failed behaviors while sharing a common vision-language backbone, enabling efficient failure-aware policy learning with limited parameter overhead. During sampling, the failure generator adaptively steers action generation away from failure-prone regions and toward more reliable success modes, with guidance strength determined by the per-diffusion-step distance between success and failure distributions. Experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain robotic manipulation tasks, covering both short- and long-horizon settings, show that AFIL consistently improves task success rates and robustness over existing VLA baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness, efficiency, and generality.

quick_skim.title: A switching proximal gradient method for constrained difference-of-convex optimization problems
quick_skim.abstract: We study difference-of-convex optimization problems with several composite inequality constraints and develop a majorization-guided switching proximal gradient (MGSPG) method. Specifically, at each feasible outer point, quadratic majorization and linearization yield a strongly convex composite surrogate problem. To solve this surrogate approximately, we employ a switching proximal gradient (SPG) method, which takes a proximal gradient step for the objective when the current point is nearly feasible and for a most violated constraint otherwise. This construction requires neither projection onto the joint surrogate feasible set nor multiplier computation. By establishing a common invariant ball and using an increasing weight argument, we obtain an \(O(τ^{-1})\) inner complexity bound for SPG. Building on this bound, we show that, under boundedness of the feasible level set and a uniform Slater condition for the surrogates, MGSPG finds an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT point in \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer iterations and \(O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) selected component proximal gradient updates. Numerical experiments on SCAD-constrained and groupwise-constrained regression problems demonstrate the viability and computational efficiency of our method compared with existing optimization algorithms.
